name: Lower Valley of the Awash
description: In Ethiopia's Awash valley, fossil beds have yielded some of the richest clues to how humans evolved, with remains at least 4 million years old. The most famous find came in 1974, when 52 bone fragments were pieced together into the skeleton nicknamed Lucy. The river runs through dry, open country toward the Djibouti border, and its ancient sediments still give up the bones of our distant ancestors.
